newsitem.title: GERMANY: U.S. soldiers accused of sex abuse in Germany.
newsitem.headline: U.S. soldiers accused of sex abuse in Germany.

text.p: The U.S. army said on Friday that two soldiers had been charged with raping female recruits and a third with sexual harassment at a training base in Germany.

The announcement came weeks after the U.S. army removed First Sergeant George Watlington as head of the Darmstadt training centre, where 11 women soldiers said they were sexually assaulted or harassed by male sergeants from last November to January.

A statement by U.S. commanders based in Heidelberg said Sergeant First Class Julius Davis, based at the 440th Signal Battalion in Darmstadt, was accused on a number of charges including six counts of rape and one of forced sodomy, they said.
Sergeant Paul Fuller, of the 77th Maintenance Company, Babenhausen in Germany, was accused o charges that included three counts of rape and three counts of forced sodomy, it said.

The two men, who were also accused of sexual harassment, were being held at the European Regional Confinement Facility, Coleman Barracks in Mannheim, partly for alleged interference in an investigation into them.
Staff Sergeant Robert Robinson, of the 596th Maintenance Company in Darmstadt, was charged with sexual harassment and fraternisation.

The commanders said they "would spare no effort to foster a command climate that ensures leaders, soldiers, civilian workers and family members live and work in an environment where dignity and respect are accorded to all."
They said the alleged victims were receiving support from the Victim-Witness liaison at the Darmstadt Legal Center. They did not give any other details about the accused or their alleged victims.
The charges were announced weeks after the U.S. army said it was investigating allegations of sexual harassment and abuse of female soldiers at U.S. training bases in Germany.
The investigation followed a series of scandals at U.S. army bases in the United States, including accusations of sexual misconduct at the Aberdeen Providing Ground in Maryland.
